slides.heading: Generate Document
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Strings
slides.narration: Let's solve Generate Document, an easy strings problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Can `document` be built from the multiset of characters in `characters`?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Can document be built from the multiset of characters in characters?

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: We can build the document if, for every character, we have at least as many copies available as needed.
slides.narration: We can build the document if, for every character, we have at least as many copies available as needed.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: for each doc char, count it in both strings → O(m·(n+m))
Optimal: one frequency map → O(n + m)
Fail fast as soon as a count goes negative
slides.narration: Recounting each character in both strings is quadratic. Counting the available characters once and decrementing for the document is linear, and we can stop as soon as a count goes negative.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. For each document character, decrement its count
3. If any count goes negative, return false
slides.narration: Step by step. First, count available characters. Second, for each document character, decrement its count. Third, if any count goes negative, return false.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Count the available characters first
slides.narration: We count every available character, including spaces and punctuation.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Every character was available → true
slides.narration: Every character of the document was available, so the answer is true.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We count the available characters in a map, then for each document character decrement its count and return false if it drops below zero.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n plus m. Space is O of c.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Unicode beyond ASCII → use a map
slides.narration: Matching is case-sensitive and spaces count. An empty document can always be generated.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: many documents from one pool
slides.narration: Ask about the character set. If you need to answer for many documents, reuse the counts.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: We can build the document if, for every character, we have at least as many copies available as needed.
slides.narration: To recap Generate Document: We can build the document if, for every character, we have at least as many copies available as needed. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
